children: Higher revenue and a sharp improvement in the thermal and hydro segment support Tata Power’s quarterly earnings, despite a more than threefold rise in fuel costs

Tata Power reported a 48.6 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated profit attributable to owners of the company to Rs 1,366.11 crore for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, from Rs 919.44 crore in the corresponding quarter a year ago.

Consolidated revenue from operations increased 26.3 per cent to Rs 19,635.94 crore in the second quarter of FY27 from Rs 15,544.91 crore in Q2 FY26. Total income rose 24.4 per cent to Rs 19,964.30 crore from Rs 16,050.32 crore.

Profit before tax increased 29.8 per cent to Rs 2,179.85 crore from Rs 1,679.90 crore in Q2 FY26. The company reported exceptional income of Rs 119.18 crore during the quarter, including a Rs 317.36 crore gain on derecognition of an interest in an associate. This was partly offset by a Rs 102.28 crore impairment of investment property and a Rs 95.90 crore impairment of investment in a joint venture.
Fuel Costs Rise Sharply

Tata Power's consolidated expenses increased to Rs 18,640.57 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 14,723.66 crore in the year-ago period. Fuel costs more than tripled to Rs 4,632.94 crore from Rs 1,347.06 crore. Cost of power purchased increased to Rs 6,244.99 crore from Rs 5,663.93 crore, while finance costs rose to Rs 1,384.93 crore from Rs 1,318.65 crore.

Depreciation and amortisation expense increased to Rs 1,286.55 crore from Rs 1,162.05 crore. The increase in reported profit came despite the higher cost base. Profit before regulatory deferral balances, share of profit of associates and joint ventures, exceptional items and tax stood at Rs 1,323.73 crore, compared with Rs 1,326.66 crore in Q2 FY26.
Thermal Segment Improves

The thermal and hydro segment reported a sharp improvement in its segment result, which increased to Rs 1,066.66 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 413 crore in the year-ago quarter. Revenue and net movement in regulatory deferral balances for the segment increased to Rs 5,883.14 crore from Rs 2,335.86 crore.

The renewables segment reported a segment result of Rs 1,230.14 crore, compared with Rs 1,140.14 crore a year earlier. Revenue and net movement in regulatory deferral balances increased to Rs 3,745.48 crore from Rs 3,613.11 crore.

Transmission and distribution segment results declined to Rs 986.64 crore from Rs 1,020.99 crore, despite segment revenue and net movement in regulatory deferral balances rising to Rs 11,937.26 crore from Rs 10,935.69 crore.
Mundra Plant Remains Key Factor

Tata Power's consolidated results continue to include disclosures related to its Mundra power plant. The company had temporarily suspended operations at the plant from 3 July 2025 to undertake pending overhaul activities aimed at resolving technical issues. It subsequently executed a supplementary power purchase agreement with Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam with a revised tariff and power supply framework.

The Ministry of Power allowed operations under Section 11 of the Electricity Act, 2003 from 1 April 2026. The directions were initially issued until 30 June 2026 and were subsequently extended until 30 September 2026. On 25 September 2026, the directions were further extended until 31 December 2026.
Singapore Arbitration Risk Continues

The company also faces an ongoing legal matter related to an arbitration award involving Kleros Capital Partners. The Singapore International Arbitration Centre had directed Tata Power to pay USD 490.32 million in damages, along with interest and costs. During the quarter, the Singapore International Commercial Court dismissed the company's application to set aside the awards.

An enforcement order was subsequently issued. On 6 November 2026, notices were served intimating attachment of Tata Power's shareholding in certain Singapore subsidiaries by the court-appointed sheriff.

Tata Power has filed an appeal before the Singapore Court of Appeal and is required to file its written submissions by 23 November 2026. The company is also seeking deferment of the sale of shares pending the appeal.

No adjustment has been made in the consolidated financial results for the quarter or the first half of FY27 in relation to the matter, pending the outcome of the appeal and enforcement proceedings. The auditors have drawn attention to the matter without modifying their conclusion.
Capex Puts Pressure On Cash

Tata Power generated Rs 6,136.81 crore in net cash from operating activities during the first half of FY27, compared with Rs 802.95 crore in H1 FY26. At the same time, cash outflow towards the purchase of capital assets increased to Rs 9,832.62 crore during the first half from Rs 6,853.70 crore a year earlier.

The company's debt-equity ratio stood at 1.62 times at 30 September 2026, compared with 1.58 times a year earlier. The total debt-to-total-assets ratio stood at 0.44 times. For the first half of FY27, consolidated profit attributable to owners stood at Rs 2,542.04 crore, compared with Rs 1,979.30 crore in H1 FY26. Revenue from operations increased to Rs 38,687.20 crore from Rs 33,579.98 crore.
